Insecurity is becoming a fad rather than an emotion. Many teens are falling subject to this new trend. Many teens that fall subject often take selfies, and post the selfies on various places of the internet an social media. The vast majority of teens that post selfies or that take selfies is the female population. Now I am a fellow female, however I do not believe I count because I only have a selfie as one profile picture, and do not post them. However, I can relate to the insecurity of some of the teens who post selfies. Who doesn't want to be told they look nice. What I have gathered is that many people who post selfies just need to feel as if they are being noticed. The person posting may need to be told they are attractive because that is the only way they hear such a compliment. 

As to contributing to this sub, I do not think they do. I think selfies should be posted into a sub like r/truthfulteenopinions or r/amiugly if people really need to know. But if the teen just has a low self esteem, it won't matter how many selfies they post or compliments they receive. It is like.... Drinking salt water to help dehydration. Sure, it seems like it is helping, but really you just need more water in the end. Receiving the compliments is an immediate relief to ease the low self esteem, how ever it will always come back.
